section_summary.extract_value: The Introduction situates body image as a multidimensional construct and frames the study's purpose as examining how negative (appearance dissatisfaction) and positive (body appreciation) aspects of body image relate to sexual health in an age-varied sample of adult women. The text defines body appreciation and argues it is distinct from the absence of negative body image, and no explicit study labels (e.g., 'Study 1') or methodological/sample details are provided in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: "In keeping with this new paradigm, the purpose of this study was to examine how both negative and positive aspects of body image contribute to sexual health among an agevaried sample of adult women."; "Body appreciation is defined as the degree to which one may (1) hold a favorable opinion toward one's body; (2) accept one's body despite its potential imperfections; (3) respect one's body by attending to its need and engaging in healthy behaviors; and (4) reject unrealistic body ideals portrayed by the media, thus protecting body image."
